summary: This Wikipedia article covers Venus, the second planet from the Sun, describing its physical characteristics, extreme atmosphere and surface conditions, orbit, and rotation. It also outlines its geology, volcanism, craters, internal structure and lack of a magnetic dynamo, along with the note that the page continues into observation history, search for life, and human exploration. The clipped content stops mid-sentence in the magnetic field section, so later sections are not included.
one_line: Wikipedia article on Venus, the second planet from the Sun, covering its extreme atmosphere, surface geology, volcanism, and internal structure.
key_facts: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and is the closest in mass and size to Earth.
Venus's atmosphere is 96.5% carbon dioxide and 3.5% nitrogen, with a surface pressure of 93 bar (9.3 MPa).
The mean surface temperature of Venus is 737 K (464 °C; 867 °F).
Venus takes 224.7 Earth days to orbit the Sun, and its rotation is retrograde.
Venus has no moons; it is one of two planets in the Solar System with no moons.
Venus has a diameter of 12,103.6 km, only 638.4 km less than Earth's.
About 80% of the Venusian surface is covered by smooth, volcanic plains.
Maxwell Montes, the highest mountain on Venus, lies on Ishtar Terra and its peak is 11 km above the average surface elevation.
Venus has 167 large volcanoes over 100 km across, and more than 85,000 volcanoes have been identified and mapped.
The Venusian surface is estimated to be 300–600 million years old, indicating a global resurfacing event.
Venus lacks an internal dynamo; its weak induced magnetosphere is caused by interaction between the ionosphere and the solar wind.
Clouds of mainly sulfuric acid reflect about 70% of the sunlight that falls on them back into space.
In 1961, Venera 1 became the first interplanetary flight, targeting Venus.
Venera 7 made the first soft landing on another planet in 1970.
